title: Revenue recognition: shared capacity, credits, and contract modifications guidance
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:
This guidance defines how Redwood recognizes revenue for multi-component contracts involving hosted API usage, Dedicated reserved capacity, Marketplace/partner credits, and post-signature contract modifications. It clarifies allocation, timing of recognition, treatment of customer credits/refunds, and the operational handoffs required between Sales, Legal, Revenue Operations, and Finance.

Scope:
- Applies to all customer contracts and amendments executed by Redwood that include one or more of: hosted API usage, Redwood Dedicated reservations, marketplace partner credits or co-sell credits, committed discounts, or one-time professional services tied to capacity onboarding.
- Does NOT replace product-specific pricing policy or procurement approvals; it complements existing contract intake and billing flows.

Definitions:
- Performance obligation: Distinct good or service promised to the customer (e.g., hosted API access, dedicated GPU pool capacity, initial on-prem packaging).
- Committed capacity (Dedicated): Customer-reserved monthly GPU hours or throughput capacity covered by a term commitment.
- Marketplace/partner credit: Third-party or Redwood-issued credit applied to customer billing (may be promotional, referral, or contractual offset).
- Contract modification: Any signed change to price, scope, or term (including addenda, SOWs, amendment agreements).

Principles and high-level rules:
1) Identify performance obligations and allocation basis
   - Map contract line items to discrete performance obligations: hosted API (consumable per-token), Dedicated reservation (capacity commitment), professional services (time-and-materials or fixed deliverable).
   - Use transaction price allocation where multiple obligations exist. Primary allocation order: (a) standalone sales price for Dedicated commitments, (b) observable market price for hosted API consumption, (c) residual allocation to professional services.

2) Timing of recognition
   - Hosted API usage: Recognize as usage occurs (over time) — performance delivery is continuous.
   - Dedicated reserved capacity: Recognize ratably over the committed term unless bill-and-handle or service is delivered upfront with transfer of control to customer (rare).
   - One-time professional services: Recognize based on completion method (input or output) consistent with how value transfers.

3) Contract modifications and reallocation
   - Evaluate modification as either: (A) separate contract (if new goods/services at standalone price) or (B) modification of existing contract.
   - For modifications that change committed capacity or term pricing, recast the remaining transaction price and reallocate to remaining performance obligations prospectively.

4) Marketplace and partner credits
   - If credit is a reimbursement of customer consideration (e.g., vendor-level rebate), treat as a reduction of transaction price and reduce revenue accordingly when the related revenue would be recognized.
   - If credit is consideration from a third party for marketing/referral (i.e., Redwood receives cash or credit and owes nothing to the customer), recognize as other revenue when earned and not net against customer revenue.
   - For credits applied to invoices after revenue recognition, record a contra-revenue adjustment in the period the credit is applied and ensure memo entry that ties to the originating contract/order.

Operational procedures (step-by-step):
A) Pre-signature (Sales / Legal / RevOps checklist)
   1. Sales submits proposed commercial term sheet into RevOps intake: include committed capacity metrics (GPU hours, SLOs), discount schedules, marketplace/partner credits, and termination/true-up terms.
   2. RevOps assigns contract template and records preliminary allocation of standalone selling prices (SSPs) in CPQ.
   3. Legal reviews for change of scope or special refund/credit language and flags revenue-sensitive clauses to Finance.

B) Post-signature (Finance / Revenue Operations)
   1. RevOps creates a contract record in the Revenue Contract Registry (RCR) with: performance obligations, term dates, billing cadence, and listed credits.
   2. Finance validates allocation model: ensure Dedicated commitments are allocated ratably across term unless explicit acceptance criteria indicate earlier recognition.
   3. If marketplace credits are present, classify credit type (reimbursement vs. third-party consideration) and record offset vs. revenue or other income accordingly.

C) Monthly accounting cadence
   1. Invoice generation: Billing team generates invoices per contract terms. For recurring Dedicated commitments, invoices should reflect committed amounts and show separate lines for credits/offsets.
   2. Usage true-up: If committed usage exceeded or underutilized, run true-up workflow on day 5 of the following month:
      a. Pull usage delta report (usage vs. commit).
      b. Apply true-up invoices or credit memos as specified in contract.
      c. Recognize revenue adjustments in the month when the delta is billed or credited.

D) Contract amendment handling (example workflow)
   1. Amendment submitted to RevOps with redlines, new pricing, and effective date.
   2. Finance reviews for whether the amendment should be accounted as separate contract or a modification. Provide written accounting treatment memo to RevOps within 3 business days.
   3. If modification requires reallocation: compute incremental transaction price, update RCR, and adjust revenue schedules prospectively.

Examples and worked calculations:
- Example 1: Dedicated reservation only
  Contract: Customer pays $120,000 for 12-month Dedicated pool (fixed monthly billing $10,000). No other obligations.
  Recognition: Recognize $10,000 revenue per month.

- Example 2: Mixed Dedicated + Hosted API consumption with discount
  Contract: $60,000 Dedicated (6 months) + hosted API estimated usage $12,000; total transaction price $72,000. SSPs: Dedicated = $50,000, Hosted = $22,000 (based on observable list prices). Allocate 50k/22k proportion. Recognition: dedicated over term ratably; hosted recognized as consumed.

- Example 3: Marketplace credit applied by partner to customer invoice
  If partner issues a $5,000 rebate that reimburses customer payments (partner pays Redwood which reduces what Redwood invoices customer): treat as reduction of transaction price and reduce revenue by $5,000 in the period the related revenue is recognized. If partner pays Redwood directly but the arrangement is for Redwood’s marketing activities, classify as other income.

Journal entry examples (simplified):
- When recognizing monthly Dedicated revenue:
  DR Accounts Receivable $10,000
  CR Revenue — Dedicated $10,000

- When applying a credit memo post-recognition (contra-revenue adjustment):
  DR Sales Returns & Allowances (contra-rev) $5,000
  CR Accounts Receivable / Cash $5,000

Controls, approvals, and ownership:
- Sales: responsible for accurate commercial terms entry; must attach pricing rationale and SSP evidence to every non-standard deal.
- Legal: approve customer-facing amendments and any credit/refund language.
- RevOps: create and maintain RCR, ensure billing config maps to allocation, and tag credits with type.
- Finance (Revenue Accounting): final sign-off on accounting treatment, entries, and monthly close adjustments. Provide approval memo for any modification that changes treatment.

Required attachments and evidence (to be stored in RCR):
- Signed contract and amendments (PDF).
- CPQ quote and rate cards used to derive SSPs.
- Usage reports and true-up reconciliations (CSV).
- Partner credit agreements or evidence of payment (for third-party consideration classification).

Escalation and exception handling:
- If Finance and RevOps disagree on modification accounting, escalate to Head of Finance with written positions within 2 business days.
- Material adjustments (> $250k or >10% of expected contract value) require Controller review and disclosure in monthly close notes.

Reporting needs and dashboards:
- Revenue team will publish a monthly "Commitment and Credits" dashboard including: active committed ARR from Dedicated, monthly variance (usage vs. committed), credits applied (by type), and modification impacts.
- Key SLOs for the process: contract intake to RCR creation < 3 business days; amendment accounting memo < 3 business days; true-up processing < 7 days after month close.

Appendix A — Quick decision guide (flow):
1. Is the amendment changing scope or price materially? -> Yes: Finance review.
2. Is the added item sold at SSP? -> Yes: May be separate contract.
3. Is credit from partner reimbursing customer payments? -> Yes: Reduce transaction price.

Appendix B — Quick reference table (high level):
| Line item type | Typical allocation | Recognition timing | Treatment of partner credit |
| Hosted API usage | SSP per-token | As used (over time) | Reduce transaction price if reimbursing |
| Dedicated reservation | SSP = committed price | Ratably over term | Credits reduce transaction price unless third-party marketing income |
| Professional services | Separate if distinct deliverable | Completion or progress | N/A |
